coach_says: Your TSB is very high (+43) but the recovery signals disagree — HRV is low, resting HR is rising, and readiness is 32 with Garmin flagging STRAINED. So the week protects your committed Tuesday double, keeps everything around it genuinely easy, and adds one tempo session on Friday to attack the -547 aerobic-high shortage without adding more anaerobic load (which is already over target). The conference override shaped Thursday through Sunday into morning MTB only, so gym is skipped this week — resume Workout A next Monday. Watch morning HRV: if it hasn't rebounded by Friday, downgrade the tempo intervals to steady Zone 2.

days.details: 45 min restorative/yin-style flow at lunch. Focus: hips, hamstrings, thoracic spine, and 5 min of diaphragmatic breathing to finish. No loading today — readiness is 32 with ~30h recovery time outstanding, and tomorrow is your committed double hard day. Weather is drizzly and windy anyway. Goal: arrive at Tuesday as fresh as possible.

days.session: AM hills ride + PM hard MTB group ride (committed double)
days.details: AM (60 min | Threshold hills | Zone 3-4): Warm up 15 min Zone 2, then 3 x 8 min sustained climbing at Zone 3 high to Zone 4 low (RPE 7-8), 5 min easy spinning between efforts, cool down 10 min Zone 1. Ride the climbs seated and steady — this targets your aerobic-high shortage, so avoid surging above threshold. Wet and windy forecast: mudguards, layers, and pick sheltered climbs. PM (90 min | Hard MTB group ride | Zone 4-5 bursts): Non-negotiable committed session. Ride it as it comes, but given anaerobic load is already above target, resist contesting every sprint — sit in where you can. Fuel well between sessions (carbs within 30 min of the AM ride) and prioritise an early night.

Lunch swim, ~1000m total, purely recovery flush after yesterday's double. Warmup: 200m easy freestyle, focus on long strokes. Main set: 4 x 100m easy freestyle at RPE 3-4 with 20s rest, then 4 x 50m drill (catch-up or single-arm) with 15s rest. Cooldown: 200m very easy mixed strokes. No hard efforts at all — this is circulation and range of motion before travelling to the conference this evening. Wettest day of the week, so the pool is the right call.

90 min | Aerobic base | Zone 2, RPE 3-4, conversational throughout. Morning ride within the 2h conference window. Choose flowing, non-technical trails and keep power/HR capped in Zone 2 — spin up climbs seated, no punchy efforts. Yesterday's double plus low readiness means today is about easy aerobic volume only. Wet forecast: allow extra time for bike cleaning, and cut to 60 min if trails are badly waterlogged.

110 min | Tempo — aerobic-high development | Zone 3. Warm up 20 min Zone 2 with 3 x 30s leg-speed spins. Main set: 3 x 12 min at Zone 3 (RPE 6, controlled breathing, sustainable) with 6 min easy spinning between. Use fire roads or steady climbs so efforts stay smooth — no anaerobic spikes. Cool down 15-20 min Zone 1. Clearest weather of the week, so make this the quality ride. This directly targets the aerobic-high load gap. Checkpoint: if morning HRV is still low, convert efforts to steady Zone 2 and ride 2 hours easy instead.

75 min | Recovery/easy aerobic | Zone 1-2, RPE 2-3. Morning ride, well within the 2h limit. Relaxed trail riding — soft-pedal, high cadence, freewheel the descents, no efforts. Drizzle and wind forecast, so keep it short and enjoyable rather than forcing distance. This buffers recovery between Friday's tempo work and Sunday's longer ride.

days.session: Long endurance MTB before travelling home
days.details: 2.5 hrs | Long aerobic endurance | Zone 2, RPE 3-4. The one day the override allows a longer ride — use it for steady aerobic volume. Ride continuously in Zone 2, seated climbing, minimal coasting, fuelling every 45 min (60g carbs/hr). No intervals: the week's quality quota is filled by Tuesday and Friday, and this keeps the week close to 80/20. Finish with enough margin to clean up and travel home in the evening. If legs feel heavy after the week, cap it at 2 hours.
